Subject: Defining success criteria for pilot with Redwood

Karthik —

- Concrete acceptance tests we can run (what we measure and thresholds).
- A short timeline (we're targeting a 4–6 week pilot window).
- Any required evidence for security & compliance reviewers (SOC2 artifacts, data handling notes).

If you can reply with a first-draft MAP and acceptance matrix we can review internally tomorrow. I copied procurement for invoicing/checkpoints.

Subject: RE: Defining success criteria for pilot with Redwood

Emily — appreciate the clear asks. Below is a concise MAP + acceptance matrix (first draft). I kept it intentionally minimal so IT/procurement can review quickly.

Mutual Action Plan (summary)
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for triage routing at production-like scale and quality so Allwell can commit to a phased rollout.
- Pilot scope: 8k daily requests, 3 weeks ramp, 1 week stability window (total 4 weeks target).

Exit gates (all required for formal "pass")
1) Accuracy: Model routing/intent accuracy >= 91% on evaluation set and no regression > 3% vs baseline in production A/B.
2) Latency: Inference p95 end-to-end (app -> Redwood -> app) <= 350 ms during steady-state load.
3) Reliability: Error rate <= 0.5% and availability >= 99.0% during stability window.
4) Data & security checklist: SOC2 in-scope evidence reviewed + no blocked data-flow patterns for ePHI.
5) Operational readiness: Runbook for rollback, KV-cache warm start validated, and monitoring alerts wired to Allwell ops.

Acceptance tests (pass criteria & how to measure)
- Functional: 1,000 labeled samples run through the deployed model; accept if accuracy >= 91% and F1 drop vs baseline <= 3 points. (Test harness: shared eval set + script)
- Performance: 30-minute steady-state soak at 1.2x expected qps; measure p50/p95/p99 and tail latencies. Pass if p95 <= 350 ms and no p99 spikes > 800 ms for more than 1 minute.
- Load: Gradual ramp to peak qps (8k/day distribution) with no degraded throughput.
- Security: Provide SOC2 Type II summary, data flow diagram, and confirmation that request payloads are not persisted beyond configured retention.
- Integration smoke: End-to-end sample flow from Allwell sandbox hitting the Redwood endpoint and returning correct routing for 100 synthetic cases with pass rate >= 95%.

Deliverables & owners
- Acceptance matrix (attached) — Karthik (Redwood)
- Deployment runbook + monitoring config — Monica (Redwood)
- Performance tuning notes & kernel selection doc — Markus (Redwood)
- Allwell validation run and evidence upload — Emily / Allwell ops

Attachments: pilot-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (matrix + test scripts), MAP-Allwell-Redwood-2026.pdf (one-pager)

Next step: If this looks good, propose a kickoff on Thursday 07/30 to align on test harness and ingestion keys.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Looping in with a small product/perf note — I want to flag two minor edits to the thresholds so they're practical for the initial pilot and still meaningful:

- Latency: recommend p95 <= 400 ms during initial ramp and target 350 ms for the stability window. The difference buys us time to tune quantization and batching configs.
- Reliability: raise availability target to 99.5% for the stability sign-off (we can commit to an SLA conversation later).

I'll prepare the kernel/quantization plan and a short test schedule for the 3-week ramp so Monica can bring the monitoring playbook in sync.

On approach: we'll provide two measurement runs — a baseline run (current routing) and pilot run — to show delta metrics clearly. That will make the acceptance decision data-driven.

-Markus

Thanks — this is very helpful and much clearer than our internal draft. A few notes from IT and procurement:

- Latency: we can accept the two-stage approach. For formal pass we want p95 <= 400 ms for the ramp and p95 <= 350 ms for the stability window.
- Availability: procurement requests 99.5% availability in the stability window as Markus suggested.
- Security: please include a short statement that request payloads will not be stored in logs and that KMS integration is available for keys.
- Procurement asked about billing milestones tied to acceptance. We prefer: 25% on kickoff, 50% on successful completion of stability window & evidence, 25% on formal go-live (post-rollout). Procurement copied here for contract language.

If Redwood can update the matrix with these small edits, Allwell is ready to kickoff on Thu 07/30 at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Emily
